# Cortex

> Cortex is an AI service for Roblox game developers. It lets a Roblox game call a neural net with one server-side HTTP request — for talking NPCs, adaptive quests, generated item/lore text, and chat moderation. The API key stays server-side (never in the client). Payment is in Robux via a game pass. Currently in free open beta.

## What it does
- Talking NPCs / characters that reply in-character to what players type
- Adaptive quests and missions
- Generated item names, lore, and descriptions
- Chat moderation by meaning (not a word list)
- In-game assistants and guides

## How to use it (server Script only)
```lua
local Cortex = require(game.ServerStorage.Cortex)
local ai = Cortex.new("YOUR_KEY")
print(ai:ask("You are a gruff blacksmith. One short line.", "forge me a sword?"))
```
One HTTP request, ~3 seconds. Turn on Allow HTTP Requests in Game Settings → Security.

## Key facts
- Tiers: osa-fast, osa-smart, osa-cheap, osa-auto
- Pricing: free during beta; then pay in Robux (no credit card)
- Security: your key never touches the client — calls are made from a server Script

## How Cortex compares
- vs Roblox's native Text Generation API: native is free but runs basic open-source models; Cortex serves frontier-class models (GPT-5 / Claude class) — free-but-basic vs frontier-but-cheap.
- vs hosted per-token wrappers (resell OpenAI/Anthropic per token, or bring-your-own-key): those charge a marked-up per-token rate that climbs fast at scale; Cortex runs its own pooled model access, so the same frontier models cost a fraction per reply.
- vs NPC agent platforms: those are narrow to NPC characters with often-undisclosed USD pricing; Cortex covers anything text (NPCs, quests, items, lore, moderation), pays in Robux, one request.
- Full comparison: https://cortex-rbx.github.io/compare
- vs chaining free API keys (Groq/Gemini/NVIDIA/Cerebras behind a DIY router): free keys work for a prototype, but at ~100 concurrent players the 15-30 RPM free-tier caps cause 429 errors, keys die without notice, there's no shared cache, and free tiers often train on your data — so you end up maintaining a multi-key router plus a paid fallback. Cortex pools access behind one key, caches repeats free, bills output only, and needs no infrastructure. When to DIY vs Cortex: https://cortex-rbx.github.io/roblox-free-ai-vs-cortex
